cli:-accesscode.what: Steam UI (steamui.so) switch, probably supplying an access/activation code at startup; the related `-accesscode=` form is forwarded by the client's command-line handler alongside `-login`/`-applaunch`, so it likely takes `-accesscode=<code>`. Purpose not confirmed.

cli:-all_languages.what: VGUI localization (vgui2_s.so) flag: load localization files for all languages instead of only the current `%language%` one, probably for translation testing. Presence flag.

cli:-allosarches.what: Bootstrapper flag: request client packages for every OS architecture rather than only the running one, typically for mirroring or testing the package manifest. Presence flag.

cli:-allosvers.what: Bootstrapper flag: request client packages for every OS version in the manifest, not just the current one. Presence flag; pairs with `-allosarches`.

cli:-allowbrowserviewunderlays.what: steamwebhelper flag (Valve: allow browser view underlays). It is the webhelper-side counterpart of `-cef-allow-browser-underlays`, which steamclient passes through when launching the webhelper.

cli:-allowremotediscovery.what: steamclient.so flag for the Remote Play / In-Home Streaming client manager: probably allows this client to be discovered by, or to discover, remote Steam clients. It sits next to the opposite switch `-preventsteamdiscovery`.

cli:-alwaysrelaunch.what: Bootstrapper flag: always re-exec the client after the update step, even when nothing changed. Presence flag.

cli:-applaunch.what: Launch a game when Steam starts: `steam -applaunch <appid> [game args...]`. It is handled by the Steam UI command-line dispatcher (CSteamDoc::ExecCommandLine) and also forwarded to an already running instance.

cli:-arch.what: Registered in steamclient/chromehtml next to the CEF switches, and the bootstrapper uses it to request packages for a given architecture. Probably takes an architecture value such as `-arch x64`; the client also appends `&ARCH=%s` to the Steam UI URL.

cli:-batterytestmode.what: Test hook in the steamclient system manager. It makes the reported battery percentage cycle rapidly instead of reading SDL_GetPowerInfo, so the battery UI can be exercised on Deck-style devices.

cli:-bigpicture.what: Start the client directly in Big Picture mode (steamui.so). Related switches: `-tenfoot` (alias), `-gamepadui` and `-nobigpicture` (force off).

cli:-bootreserve.what: steamclient.so flag, probably reserving a block of disk space at boot as a safety buffer (sized by `-bootreservesizemb`). Evidence is only adjacent strings.

cli:-bootreservesizemb.what: steamclient.so switch that probably takes a size in MB for the `-bootreserve` reservation (`-bootreservesizemb <MB>`). Evidence is only the name.

cli:-bootstrapperproxy.what: Bootstrapper switch that takes an argument: an HTTP proxy used for the bootstrapper's own package downloads.

cli:-buildid.what: steamsysinfo option: `-buildid <id>`, the build identifier attached to crash reports. It is used together with `-steamid`, `-logdir`, `-query` and `-out-file`.

cli:-cafeapplaunch.what: steamclient.so switch: launch apps in a cyber-cafe (internet cafe licensing) context. Presence flag.

cli:-candidates.what: steamclient.so debug flag: log the libjingle ICE candidates for local P2P/streaming connections as they are processed.

cli:-ccsyntax.what: VGUI localization debug flag: log details about each localized string file and token that is loaded. Useful together with `-language`.

cli:-cef-allow-browser-underlays.what: CEF switch: allow steamwebhelper to create BrowserView underlays. steamclient forwards it to the webhelper as `-allowbrowserviewunderlays`.

cli:-cef-disable-breakpad.what: CEF switch: disable Breakpad crash reporting in steamwebhelper.

cli:-cef-disable-browser-underlays.what: CEF switch: turn off BrowserView underlay support in steamwebhelper. It is the opposite of `-cef-force-browser-underlays`.

cli:-cef-disable-gpu.what: CEF switch: disable GPU use in steamwebhelper, forcing software rendering and compositing. This is a common workaround for black or flickering Steam windows caused by driver problems.

cli:-cef-disable-gpu-compositing.what: CEF switch: disable GPU-accelerated compositing in steamwebhelper while other GPU use stays enabled.

cli:-cef-disable-gpu-sandbox.what: CEF switch: disable the Chromium GPU-process sandbox in steamwebhelper.

cli:-cef-disable-hang-timeouts.what: CEF switch: disable Chromium's GPU and renderer hang watchdogs, so a stalled webhelper process isn't killed. Useful when debugging the webhelper.

cli:-cef-disable-hevc.what: CEF switch: disable HEVC (H.265) video support in steamwebhelper.

cli:-cef-disable-js-logging.what: CEF switch: stop logging Steam UI JavaScript console messages to the console and to the webhelper log file.

cli:-cef-disable-logging.what: CEF switch: disable CEF/Chromium logging from steamwebhelper.

cli:-cef-disable-occlusion.what: CEF switch: disable Chromium's window-occlusion detection, so hidden or covered Steam windows keep rendering.

cli:-cef-disable-renderer-restart.what: CEF switch: don't automatically restart a crashed renderer process for an existing browser.

cli:-cef-disable-safe-shutdown-workaroun.what: CEF switch: turn off the safe browser shutdown workaround that is otherwise applied on Linux with NVIDIA drivers. It is forwarded to the webhelper as `-disable_safe_shutdown_workaround`; the env var `STEAM_DISABLE_BROWSER_SHUTDOWN_WORKAROUND` has the same effect.

cli:-cef-disable-sandbox.what: CEF switch: disable Chromium sandboxing in steamwebhelper. `-no-cef-sandbox` is registered next to it as an equivalent.

cli:-cef-disable-seccomp-sandbox.what: CEF switch: disable only the Linux seccomp-bpf layer of the Chromium sandbox.

cli:-cef-disable-site-isolation.what: CEF switch: disable Chromium per-site process isolation, which reduces the number of renderer processes.

cli:-cef-disable-touch-focus-workaround.what: CEF switch: turn off the touch-input browser-focus workaround. It is forwarded to the webhelper as `-disabletouchfocusworkaround`.

cli:-cef-disable-xcomposite-workaround.what: CEF switch: turn off the glcomposer/XComposite workaround that is applied automatically for some video drivers.

cli:-cef-enable-debugging.what: CEF switch: enable Chromium remote debugging (DevTools protocol) on localhost:8080 by default; the port can be changed with `-devtools-port`. Afterwards you can attach Chrome DevTools to the Steam UI.

cli:-cef-enable-gpu-debugging.what: CEF switch: enable Chromium GPU debugging, which runs glGetError() after every GL command. It is very slow.

cli:-cef-enable-low-delay-live-stream.what: CEF switch: reduce buffering for live video playback (e.g. Steam Broadcasts) in the webhelper.

cli:-cef-enable-vaapi.what: CEF switch: enable VA-API hardware video decoding in steamwebhelper on Linux.

cli:-cef-force-accessibility.what: CEF switch: force-enable Chromium accessibility. The webhelper is then started with `--force-renderer-accessibility`, for screen readers.

cli:-cef-force-browser-underlays.what: CEF switch: force BrowserView underlays on even where they are off by default. It is forwarded to the webhelper as `-forcebrowserviewunderlays`.

cli:-cef-force-gpu.what: CEF switch: force GPU acceleration in steamwebhelper even where it would be disabled (e.g. by the blocklist).

cli:-cef-force-gpu-blocklist.what: CEF switch: force Chromium's GPU driver blocklist on, so blocklisted GPUs fall back to software.

cli:-cef-force-hw-video-decode.what: CEF switch: force hardware-accelerated video decoding in steamwebhelper.

cli:-cef-force-occlusion.what: CEF switch: force Chromium window-occlusion detection on. It is the opposite of `-cef-disable-occlusion`.

cli:-cef-force-opaque-backgrounds.what: CEF switch: force opaque, non-transparent backgrounds for CEF browsers. Possibly a workaround for compositors that render transparency badly.

cli:-cef-force-sandbox.what: CEF switch: force the Chromium sandbox on even where Steam would disable it.

cli:-cef-full-memory-crash-report.what: CEF switch: write full-memory crash dumps for steamwebhelper crashes instead of minidumps.

cli:-cef-log-sandbox.what: CEF switch: enable logging of Chromium sandbox decisions in steamwebhelper.

cli:-cef-use-vulkan.what: CEF switch: run Chromium's ANGLE graphics layer on its Vulkan backend instead of the default GL backend.

cli:-cef-verbose-js-logging.what: CEF switch: log Steam UI JavaScript console events verbosely. It is forwarded to the webhelper as `-verbosejslogging`.

cli:-cef-verbose-logging.what: CEF switch: enable verbose Chromium/CEF logging in steamwebhelper.

cli:-cef-verbose-modules.what: CEF switch: enable verbose logging for selected CEF modules. It probably takes a module list in Chromium `--vmodule` style; the format is not confirmed.

cli:-child-update-ui.what: Internal bootstrapper flag: marks a process as the forked child that draws the update/progress UI. It is not meant to be passed by hand.

cli:-child-update-ui-socket.what: Internal bootstrapper switch: `-child-update-ui-socket <fd>` gives the update-UI child the IPC socket for talking to the parent bootstrapper.

cli:-chromeos.what: ChromeOS (Borealis) integration flag read by tier0 platform detection. It makes Steam behave as the ChromeOS build.

cli:-chromeosverbose.what: ChromeOS (Borealis) verbose flag: more logging for ChromeOS-specific paths, such as the disk-space management that calls `/usr/bin/crosdisk` (BEnsureDiskSpaceAvailable / BReleaseExcessDiskSpace).

cli:-clearbeta.what: Bootstrapper flag: leave the client beta and return to the stable branch by removing `package/beta`. Platform-specific branch prefixes (`steamdeck_`, `steampal_`, `chromeos_`) are handled near it.

cli:-clientbeta.what: `-clientbeta <branch>`: run a different client beta branch for this session only, without changing the saved `package/beta`. The log says "Overriding client beta for this session ... (clientbeta flag)".

cli:-compat.what: VGUI flag, probably a compatibility mode for UI DPI scaling (it sits next to the `DPIScaling` registry value and `-nodpiscale`).

cli:-compat-disable-filtering.what: Steam Play/compat tools switch: show compatibility tools/runtimes that are normally hidden (unlisted) in the selection UI.

cli:-compat-force-slr.what: Steam Play switch: force the Steam Linux Runtime 1.0 (scout) container on or off by default for native Linux games, instead of the legacy LD_* library-path setup. Probably takes a 0/1 value.

cli:-complete_install_via_http.what: steamclient.so switch: run install-completion steps over HTTP by default instead of the CM connection. Presence flag.

cli:-console.what: Steam UI flag: enable the developer console in the client (Console tab / `steam://open/console`), where the concommands documented here are typed. `-noconsole` is the opposite.

cli:-controllertypeoverride.what: steamclient.so controller switch that probably takes a controller type value and overrides the detected controller type. It sits next to `-forcedeckcontroller` and haptic convars.

cli:-debug_steamapi.what: steamclient.so switch: log Steam API (steamworks interface) calls made by games. Output probably goes to the `apiwarning_log`/steam_api log.

cli:-debugamf.what: Steam UI switch: enable AMD AMF video-encoder debug logging. This affects Remote Play and game recording encode paths.

cli:-debugbreak.what: Low-level (tier0) debug flag read by the bootstrapper, crashhandler, steamservice and others: trigger a debugger break at startup so a debugger can attach. Presence flag.

cli:-debugoutputlogs.what: Mirror log output to the debug output/console as well as the log files. It is read by the bootstrapper, client, overlay and webhelper; `log_files_always_flush` and `STEAM_CLIENT_LOG_FOLDER` sit next to it.

cli:-deckard.what: tier0 platform flag named after the hardware codename Deckard (related to `-steamframe`). It makes the client behave as that device. Exact effect unknown.

cli:-delaypageload.what: steamwebhelper switch, probably delaying the initial page load in the webhelper (e.g. to give time to attach a debugger). Evidence is only the name.

cli:-dev.what: Developer mode: enables developer log output and dev features across the bootstrapper, client, UI and overlay. Examples are extra HTML context-menu items (View Source, Open DevTools, Inspect Element), the WebUI transport server-status endpoint, and devkit controller hooks.

cli:-devsites.what: Point the client's web pages (store, community, etc.) at Valve's local development websites instead of production. Used together with `-devsiteshost`.

cli:-devsiteshost.what: `-devsiteshost <hostname>`: build dev site domains such as `store.<hostname>.steam.dev` for `-devsites`. This is Valve-internal.

cli:-devtools-port.what: `-devtools-port <port>`: sets the Chromium remote-debugging port of steamwebhelper (passed as `--remote-debugging-port=%s`, bound to 127.0.0.1 with `--remote-allow-origins=*`). The default is 8080. Use it with `-cef-enable-debugging`.

cli:-disable-libusb.what: Disable the steamclient controller support for devices that need exclusive USB (libusb) access. It is the opposite of `-enable-libusb`.

cli:-disable-overlay-gpu-pri.what: Overlay switch: don't raise steamwebhelper's GPU scheduling priority while the in-game overlay is visible. The delay between priority changes is set by `-overlay-gpu-pri-delay`.

cli:-disable-overlay-wait-for-cef-frame.what: Overlay switch: don't wait for a pending CEF frame to finish rendering before presenting while the overlay is visible. Possibly reduces stalls at the cost of stale or partial overlay frames.

cli:-disable-winh264.what: Windows-only CEF switch: don't load winh264.dll for H.264 decoding. It has no effect on Linux.

cli:-disable_broadcast_webrtc.what: steamclient.so flag: disable the WebRTC transport for Steam Broadcasting sessions (`Broadcast.BeginBroadcastSession`). Presence flag.

cli:-disable_safe_shutdown_workaround.what: steamwebhelper flag: skip the safe browser shutdown workaround (logs "Skipping safe browser shutdown workaround: disabled"). Same as setting `STEAM_DISABLE_BROWSER_SHUTDOWN_WORKAROUND`; the client sets it from `-cef-disable-safe-shutdown-workaround`.

cli:-disablehighdpi.what: CEF switch: disable high-DPI scaling support in steamwebhelper.

cli:-disablejslogging.what: steamwebhelper switch: disable file and console logging of JS console events. This is the webhelper-side form of `-cef-disable-js-logging`.

cli:-disablelauncherservice.what: steamclient.so switch: don't start the `steam-runtime-launcher-service` helper process. That process lets commands be run inside a game's pressure-vessel container for debugging.

cli:-disablepartnerlicenses.what: Valve/partner dev switch: disable automatically granted partner licenses. Valve warns that this affects all web and client sessions of the account, so don't use it with several active clients.

cli:-disablerendererrestart.what: steamwebhelper switch: don't auto-restart a crashed renderer for an existing browser. This is the webhelper-side form of `-cef-disable-renderer-restart`.

cli:-disabletouchfocusworkaround.what: steamwebhelper switch: disable the touch-input focus workaround. This is the webhelper-side form of `-cef-disable-touch-focus-workaround`.

cli:-disablevulkanlayer.what: Overlay switch: when the overlay is disabled, also stop loading Steam's Vulkan overlay layer into games.

cli:-display-scale=.what: VGUI (legacy UI) switch `-display-scale=<factor>`: overrides the X11 display scale factor, which otherwise comes from things like `GDK_SCALE`. The format is assumed numeric.

cli:-download.what: Bootstrapper flag: download the client package set only, probably without installing or launching. The related strings are about package download and metrics caching.

cli:-drop.what: Steam UI command-line verb handled by CSteamDoc::ExecCommandLine together with `-applaunch`/`-install`. It probably means drag-and-drop or dropped-file handling; the meaning is unclear.

cli:-dumpvideostream.what: Remote Play debug switch: write the received game stream to disk as an elementary (raw H.264/HEVC) video file.

cli:-enable-desktop-gl-fallback.what: Steam UI switch, probably allowing a fallback to desktop OpenGL for UI rendering when the preferred path fails. It sits next to `-opengl`/`-fullscreenopengl`.

cli:-enable-devkit.what: Enable Steam devkit features in the client: the devkit service used for SteamOS/Deck game development, and app-management console commands such as `app_install`.

cli:-enable-keyring.what: CEF switch: let steamwebhelper use the Chromium/OS keyring (e.g. GNOME Keyring/KWallet) for stored secrets instead of basic storage.

cli:-enable-libusb.what: Enable steamclient controller support for devices that need exclusive USB (libusb) access, instead of the kernel/hidraw path.

cli:-enable-libusb-gamecube.what: Enable support for the Nintendo GameCube controller adapter in Wii U mode through libusb.

cli:-exitsteam.what: Ask an already running Steam to exit. The bootstrapper forwards the command line to the running instance and the Steam UI handles it in CSteamDoc::ExecCommandLine. Comparable to `-shutdown`.

cli:-failsystemcheck.what: Bootstrapper test hook: make the system requirements check fail on purpose, to test the failure dialog.

cli:-flushconfig.what: Steam UI flag, probably resetting or flushing local client configuration (for example cached UI/dialog config) at startup, much like Steam's old `steam://flushconfig`. Exact scope unconfirmed.

cli:-force-no-dbus-simulate-user-activit.what: Client/UI flag: never call the D-Bus 'simulate user activity' (screensaver inhibit / wake) method, probably for desktops where it misbehaves.

cli:-force-oobe-stage1.what: Force the first stage of the out-of-box experience (first-boot setup on Steam Deck/SteamOS) to show.

cli:-force-oobe-stage2.what: Force the second stage of the out-of-box experience (post-login setup on SteamOS/Deck) to show.

cli:-forcebrowserviewunderlays.what: steamwebhelper switch: force browser view underlays on. This is the webhelper-side form of `-cef-force-browser-underlays`.

cli:-forcecontrollerappid.what: `-forcecontrollerappid <appid>`: lock Steam Input to the controller configuration of the given app, so switching apps or context doesn't change the active config. Used for testing controller configs.

cli:-forcedeckcontroller.what: steamclient.so flag: treat the built-in controller as a Steam Deck controller, as when running on a Deck (registry markers `IsSteamDeck`). Mainly for emulating Deck input.

cli:-forceguiupdater.what: Bootstrapper flag: always use the graphical update/progress window rather than the text UI.

cli:-forcemanifestsuffix.what: Bootstrapper switch that takes an argument: override the client manifest filename suffix (`steam_client_<suffix>`) to fetch a different manifest.

cli:-forcepackagedownload.what: Bootstrapper flag: re-download the client package zips even if the cached ones look valid.

cli:-forcesteamupdate.what: Bootstrapper flag: force a client update check and apply the result at startup.

cli:-forceunsupportedos.what: Bootstrapper flag: keep running on an OS that the manifest marks as unsupported.

cli:-foreground.what: Steam UI command-line verb: bring the existing Steam window to the foreground. It is usually forwarded to the running instance.

cli:-friendsui.what: Force-load the friends UI module (friendsui.so) in the client, UI and overlay. `-nofriendsui` is the opposite.

cli:-fs_log.what: Filesystem (filesystem_stdio) switch: log file-system accesses made by the client.

cli:-fs_logbins.what: Filesystem switch: log every binary/shared library loaded while running.

cli:-fs_target.what: Filesystem switch (Valve: "Set target syntax"): probably takes a value selecting the path/target syntax used by `-fs_log` output. Format unknown.

cli:-full_memory_dump.what: Bootstrapper/crash-handler flag: write full memory dumps instead of minidumps on a crash. The related env var is `BREAKPAD_DUMP_LOCATION`.

cli:-fullscreen.what: Start Big Picture mode fullscreen. `-windowed` is the windowed counterpart.

cli:-fullscreenopengl.what: Legacy VGUI switch: use the full-screen OpenGL renderer for the UI. Probably a leftover from the old Big Picture.

cli:-gameid.what: Overlay (gameoverlayui) flag, probably `-gameid <gameid>`, telling the overlay process which game it is attached to. It is set by the client, not by users.

cli:-gameidlaunch.what: Steam UI command-line verb: launch a game by its 64-bit game ID (which covers mods and shortcuts), e.g. `-gameidlaunch <gameid>`. Compare `-applaunch`, which takes an app ID.

cli:-gameinput.what: Use Microsoft GameInput for controller input. This is Windows-only and does nothing on Linux.

cli:-gamepadui.what: Start in the gamepad UI (the Steam Deck / new Big Picture interface). On SteamOS it is used together with `-steamdeck`/`-steamos3`.

cli:-hardware-updater.what: Steam UI flag: force-enable the hardware (controller/device firmware) updater. `-no-hardware-updater` is the opposite.

cli:-holo.what: tier0 platform flag for SteamOS 3 (codename holo). It is treated the same as `-steamos3`.

cli:-hometest.what: Steam UI flag that exercises the hardware survey scheduling (SurveyDate, SurveyDateVersion, SurveyDateSteamDeckDelay) next to `-steamconsole`. Probably forces or tests the survey prompt; the effect is unclear.

cli:-html-enable-tooltips.what: Show native browser tooltips (HTML `title` attributes) in the client's HTML surfaces.

cli:-html-perf-monitor.what: Draw an HTML performance overlay (frame timing data) on webhelper-rendered surfaces in the client and overlay.

cli:-ifrunning.what: Bootstrapper/UI flag: only act (forward the command line, e.g. a `steam://` URL) if Steam is already running; don't start a new client otherwise.

cli:-inf.what: False positive: matched by the string `inf` that number formatting uses (inf/nan/%.*g). It is not a real switch.

cli:-inhibitbootstrap.what: Bootstrapper flag: skip the bootstrap/update step and start whatever client is installed. Same effect as `BootStrapperInhibitAll` in steam.cfg.

cli:-init_universe.what: steamclient.so switch, probably `-init_universe <universe>`, which picks the Steam universe (public/beta/dev) at startup. Valve-internal.

cli:-install.what: Steam UI command-line verb: start installing an app, probably `-install <appid>` (compare `-uninstall`). It is forwarded to the running instance.

cli:-installupdate.what: Bootstrapper flag: apply a pending client update that was already downloaded ("Found pending update", "Applying update...").

cli:-language.what: `-language <name>`: sets the client UI language for this run, e.g. `-language german` or `schinese`. It also chooses the bootstrapper's `steambootstrapper_<lang>.txt` strings.

cli:-led-enumerate-sysfs-all.what: Steam UI (device LED control) switch: list all LED devices under sysfs, not only the ones Steam recognises. `-testled` creates a fake LED for testing.

cli:-log_voice.what: Write voice chat data to `logs/voice_log.txt` for debugging.

cli:-logdir.what: steamsysinfo option `-logdir <dir>`: the directory where the system-info tool writes its logs.

cli:-login.what: Automatically log in a user: `-login <username> [password]`. With credentials on the command line, `-rememberpassword` acts as if 'remember my password' was ticked.

cli:-lognetapi.what: Log all P2P networking (ISteamNetworking) activity to `logs/netapi_log.txt`.

cli:-longestloc.what: Localization test switch: for each token, use the longest translation across all languages, so UI layouts can be checked for text overflow.

cli:-ltp.what: steamclient.so switch: use the legacy scheme for storing the login refresh token (JWT) on disk, e.g. under `Software\Valve\Steam\ConnectCache` in registry.vdf.

cli:-manuallyclearframes.what: gameoverlayui switch: make the overlay clear its frames to black itself, for games that don't clear the whole screen and would otherwise leave artifacts.

cli:-master_ipc_name_override.what: `-master_ipc_name_override <name>`: overrides the name of the master IPC/shared-memory channel used between the bootstrapper, client and UI. With a different name, a second, separate Steam instance can run (developer use).

cli:-net_fake_state.what: `-net_fake_state <state>`: sets the initial value of the `net_fake_state` convar, which simulates network conditions. Valid states: normal, NoLAN, CaptivePortal_Redirected, CaptivePortal_InPlace, NoInternet, NoSteam.

cli:-net_start_wifi_disabled.what: Start with Wi-Fi reported as disabled. Valve says this is useful when emulating a Steam Deck on a desktop.

cli:-no-cef-sandbox.what: Disable the Chromium sandbox in steamwebhelper; same effect as `-cef-disable-sandbox`. Useful on systems without unprivileged user namespaces.

cli:-no-child-update-ui.what: Bootstrapper flag: draw the update UI in the bootstrapper process itself instead of a forked `-child-update-ui` process.

cli:-no-dwrite.what: Windows-only: make VGUI use GDI text instead of DirectWrite. It has no effect on Linux.

cli:-no-hardware-updater.what: Steam UI flag: disable the hardware/firmware updater (controller and device firmware update prompts). `-hardware-updater` is the opposite.

cli:-no-shared-textures.what: Overlay switch: don't share GPU texture handles between the overlay and the game process; the overlay uses a copy path instead. Can work around overlay glitches with some drivers.

cli:-noassert.what: tier0 flag read by the bootstrapper, crashhandler and helpers: don't break or show dialogs on (non-fatal) asserts. Similar in purpose to the `DONT_BREAK_ON_ASSERT` setting.

cli:-nobigpicture.what: Force the normal desktop UI at startup, overriding a saved Big Picture or gamepad UI startup mode. The client logs "forcing desktopui via -nobigpicture".

cli:-nobootstrapperupdate.what: Bootstrapper flag: don't update the bootstrapper binary itself during the update step.

cli:-noconsole.what: Steam UI flag: hide or disable the developer console. It is the opposite of `-console`.

cli:-nocrashdialog.what: tier0/crash-handler flag: don't show a crash dialog when a Steam process crashes.

cli:-nocrashmonitor.what: steamclient.so flag: don't start the crash-monitor process that watches the client.

cli:-nodircheck.what: Bootstrapper flag: skip the install-directory checks, e.g. non-ASCII path and writability (`.writable`).

cli:-nodpiscale.what: VGUI flag: disable DPI scaling of the legacy VGUI UI, overriding the `DPIScaling` registry setting.

cli:-nofriendsui.what: Don't load the friends UI module (friendsui.so). The friends list and chat are then unavailable.

cli:-noipv6.what: steamclient.so flag: disable IPv6 networking and use only IPv4.

cli:-nojoy.what: Disable controller support in steamclient and in the streaming client: no SDL/HID controller enumeration, no Steam Input.

cli:-nojsreload.what: Steam UI flag: don't reload the Steam UI JavaScript when it changes, probably a developer hot-reload setting.

cli:-nopcshutdown.what: Steam UI switch: skip real PC power operations (shutdown/restart/suspend) when they are triggered from the UI, so testing Big Picture power menus doesn't power off the machine.

cli:-norepairfiles.what: Bootstrapper flag: skip repairing files that fail verification ("Skipping file repair").

cli:-noshaders.what: Disable the shader pre-caching manager (no shader cache downloads/uploads or Fossilize background processing).

cli:-noverifyfiles.what: Bootstrapper flag: skip verifying client files at startup ("Verification skipped").

cli:-offlinemode.what: Always try to start Steam in offline mode, using cached credentials.

cli:-openalldevtools.what: Open a Chrome DevTools window at launch for every HTML window: Steam UI, overlay (gamepad/desktop overlay) and friends.

cli:-opendevtools.what: Open Chrome DevTools at launch for the shared JS context, the offscreen SharedJSContext browser that hosts most Steam UI logic.

cli:-opengl.what: Legacy VGUI switch: use the OpenGL renderer for the UI.

cli:-openoverlaydevtools.what: Open Chrome DevTools automatically whenever an in-game overlay browser is created.

cli:-out-file.what: steamsysinfo option `-out-file <path>`: write the query response to a file instead of stdout.

cli:-overlay-gpu-pri-delay.what: `-overlay-gpu-pri-delay <ms>`: delay in milliseconds between changes of the webhelper GPU priority as the overlay is shown or hidden.

cli:-overlaylogging.what: Enable logging from the in-game overlay renderer, probably into gameprocess/overlay logs.

cli:-overlaytestmode.what: Force the overlay into its test mode for debugging.

cli:-overrideminos.what: Bootstrapper flag: bypass the minimum-OS-version check. Valve's bootstrapper message documents it: "You may override this check by passing -overrideminos".

cli:-pid.what: Internal switch for overlay and HTML helper processes: `-pid <pid>` is the process they watch, i.e. the game the overlay is attached to. The client passes it.

cli:-pipewire.what: Enable PipeWire-based desktop capture, used by Remote Play and recording on Linux.

cli:-pipewire-dmabuf.what: Enable PipeWire desktop capture with DMA-BUF zero-copy buffers.

cli:-pipewire-fresh-start.what: Clear all saved PipeWire capture tokens, so the user is asked again what to capture (the portal screen-share prompt).

cli:-pipewire-record-deck-ui.what: Include Steam UI elements in PipeWire captures/recordings on Steam Deck.

cli:-pretendeol.what: Steam UI test flag: pretend this OS/platform has reached end of life, to show the EOL warning UI.

cli:-pretendeol32.what: Steam UI test flag: pretend 32-bit support has reached end of life, to show the corresponding warning UI.

cli:-preventsteamdiscovery.what: steamclient.so flag: stop this client from broadcasting or being discovered by other Steam clients on the LAN (Remote Play / In-Home Streaming discovery).

cli:-private_ip_override.what: steamclient.so switch that probably takes an IP address to report as the machine's private/LAN IP, e.g. for streaming or P2P testing. Evidence is only the name.

cli:-profilestartup.what: Profile client startup: record and log startup timing for steamui, steamclient and CEF (e.g. "STARTUP SteamUI browser requested at +%.0fms").

cli:-pyrowavestats.what: Log performance of the pyrowave video encoder (used for Remote Play streaming) to `streaming_log.txt`.

cli:-query.what: steamsysinfo option `-query <command>`: picks which EChildProcessQueryCommand system-info query to run. Steam spawns steamsysinfo as a helper child process.

cli:-query-arg.what: steamsysinfo option `-query-arg <value>`: the argument for the `-query` command; its meaning depends on the query.

cli:-quicklogin.what: `-quicklogin <base>`: sets the base URL used to build quick-login URLs. A Valve dev option used with `-devsites`.

cli:-rememberpassword.what: With `-login <user> <pass>`, act as if 'Remember my password' was ticked, so a refresh token is saved.

cli:-set_locale_disable.what: Bootstrapper flag: skip the `setlocale()` call at startup (normally en_US.UTF-8 or the user locale).

cli:-setbeta.what: `-setbeta <branch>`: permanently switch the client to a beta branch by writing it to `package/beta`. The log says "Changing client beta ... (changebeta flag)".

cli:-showallbetas.what: Show all client beta branches in the beta selection UI, not only the filtered list.

cli:-shutdown.what: Tell a running Steam instance to shut down. The command line is forwarded to it and handled by CSteamDoc::ExecCommandLine.

cli:-silent.what: Start Steam silently, minimized to the system tray with no main window. The bootstrapper also respects it to keep its update UI quiet.

cli:-simulatedownloaderrors.what: Bootstrapper test hook: simulate package download failures.

cli:-simulatefatalerror.what: Bootstrapper test hook: trigger a fatal error on purpose ("Forcing a fatal error").

cli:-single_core.what: Restrict Steam (steamclient and steamservice) to the primary CPU core.

cli:-singleapp.what: Single-app mode (`-singleapp <appid>` is likely): the bootstrapper and UI run Steam as a launcher for one app, reading `launcher\appid` from config/config.vdf and erroring if it is missing. Used for branded launchers, e.g. with `-steamchina`.

cli:-sitelicense.what: steamclient.so flag: run this client as a site-license provider (internet cafe / site license host). It logs "Running as site license provider"; a convar can enable the same.

cli:-skipinitialbootstrap.what: Bootstrapper flag: skip the first-run bootstrap step.

cli:-skipstreamingdrivers.what: Remote Play switch: skip the streaming driver checks (virtual audio/input drivers) before starting a stream.

cli:-skipsystemcheck.what: Bootstrapper flag: skip system-compatibility checks, e.g. the steam-runtime requirements check and GL renderer checks such as the VirtualBox 3D-acceleration warning.

cli:-sls-skip-version-check.what: Steam UI switch: don't validate the SLS version before starting. SLS is probably Steam Link Service or a similar component; exact meaning unknown.

cli:-srt-logger-opened.what: Internal flag added by steam.sh / the bootstrapper after it opens the srt-logger (writing `logs/console-linux.txt`), so the logger isn't opened twice, including after an exit-code-42 restart.

cli:-stack=.what: tier0 switch, probably `-stack=<size>`, setting the stack size for the main/worker threads. No usage strings.

cli:steam://open/bigpicture.what: Passing the URL `steam://open/bigpicture` on the command line makes the startup-mode logic (ComputeStartupMode) start in the gamepad UI / Big Picture, like `-gamepadui`.

cli:steambeta://open/bigpicture.what: Beta-protocol form of `steam://open/bigpicture`: on the command line it forces startup in the gamepad UI / Big Picture.

cli:-steamchina.what: Bootstrapper flag: run as the Steam China (Perfect World) client, with China-specific packages and universe; often used with `-singleapp`.

cli:-steamconsole.what: Steam UI flag, probably loading `steamconsole.so` or a standalone console mode. It appears next to the survey/`-hometest` code, so the exact effect is unclear.

cli:-steamdeck.what: tier0 platform flag: run the client as if on a Steam Deck (enables Deck-specific UI and behavior). Commonly used with `-gamepadui` to emulate a Deck on desktop.

cli:-steamdeckdisplay.what: Make the client (UI, CEF, overlay) assume a Steam Deck display/panel profile. It is read by almost every component and is probably used for Deck emulation.

cli:-steamframe.what: tier0 platform flag for the Steam Frame hardware (related to the `-deckard` codename). It makes the client behave as on that device.

cli:-steamid.what: steamsysinfo option `-steamid <id>`: the Steam user identifier attached to reports.

cli:-steaminstaller.what: Steam UI command-line verb, probably used by the Steam installer to hand off to the client after installation. Exact behavior unknown.

cli:-steammachinedisplay.what: Like `-steamdeckdisplay`, but makes the client assume a Steam Machine (TV/living-room) display profile.

cli:-steamos.what: Bootstrapper and steam.sh flag: run as SteamOS. steam.sh sets `STEAMOS=1` and skips the 32-bit library check; the client enables SteamOS behavior.

cli:-steamos3.what: SteamOS 3 (holo/jupiter, i.e. Steam Deck OS) platform flag, read by steam.sh and tier0. Equivalent to `-holo`.

cli:-steampid.what: Internal gameoverlayui switch: `-steampid <pid>`, the PID of the Steam process that launched the overlay.

cli:-system-composer.what: Steam UI switch: force the system browser composer (compositing path) for Big Picture rather than Steam's own composer.

cli:-tenfoot.what: Start in Big Picture mode. This is the historical name and an alias of `-bigpicture`; the startup logic may promote it to the gamepad UI.

cli:-tesla.what: tier0 platform flag named after hardware codename Tesla. Effect unknown.

cli:-testled.what: Create a fake LED device to test the client's LED control features.

cli:-testlongoobeupdater.what: steamclient system-manager test flag: use a slow dummy updater during the OOBE ("applying dummy update", progress posts), to test the long update flow.

cli:-testoobe.what: Force the out-of-box experience flow (sets/reads `ForceOOBE`) in client, UI and CEF. Used for testing first-run setup.

cli:-testoobeupdater.what: Use a dummy updater during the OOBE, so the system-update step can be tested without a real update.

cli:-testssa.what: Force the Steam Subscriber Agreement (SSA) acceptance dialog to show.

cli:-teststoragedata.what: Steam UI test switch: show fake ('test') storage data, probably in the Storage Manager / storage settings page, so the UI can be tested without real drives.

cli:-testupdater.what: steamclient system-manager test flag: probably uses a test/dummy system updater (the SteamOS update path) instead of the real one. It sits near the battery/fan/suspend system-manager code.

cli:-textclient.what: Bootstrapper flag: use the text/console update UI (CConsoleUpdateUI) instead of the graphical update window, e.g. for headless runs.

cli:-toggle-overlay-html-mode.what: Flip the default of the new, faster overlay HTML rendering path: it turns the path off where it is on by default, and on in branches where it isn't yet the default.

cli:-uninstall.what: Steam UI command-line verb: uninstall an app, probably `-uninstall <appid>`. It is forwarded to the running client (CSteamDoc::ExecCommandLine).

cli:-use_xcomposite_workaround.what: steamwebhelper flag: capture window textures through the XComposite workaround path ("using xcomposite workaround"). Same as setting `STEAM_ENABLE_XCOMPOSITE_WORKAROUND`; the client sets it automatically for some drivers.

cli:-usepipewireaudio.what: steamclient.so switch: use the PipeWire audio backend (e.g. for voice, Remote Play or recording audio) instead of the default backend.

cli:-userchooser.what: Always show the account chooser at login, even with 0 or 1 saved accounts.

cli:-verbose.what: steamclient.so flag found next to the site-license code. It probably makes site-license provider mode log more detail; any wider effect is unknown.

cli:-verbose-computer-activity.what: Log verbosely how the client detects user/computer activity, i.e. idle vs. active (used for away status and idle-time features).

cli:-verbosejslogging.what: steamwebhelper switch: log JS console events verbosely. This is the webhelper-side form of `-cef-verbose-js-logging`.

cli:-verifyfiles.what: Bootstrapper flag: verify the checksums of all client files at startup and repair mismatches ("Verifying all file checksums"). It is also read in steamclient.so. steam.sh tries to add it after a failed runtime unpack, but a script bug means the flag never reaches the client.

cli:-vguifocus.what: VGUI debug switch: print which panel has keyboard focus. Only affects legacy VGUI panels.

cli:-vguimessages.what: VGUI debug switch: print debug output for vgui2 panel messages.

cli:-voicerelay.what: Testing switch: allow voice chat only through relay connections, with no direct P2P.

cli:-vrdisable.what: Disable SteamVR integration completely: Steam never loads the OpenVR libraries.

cli:-vrforce.what: Always run the HMD (headset) status check at startup, even if it crashed last time. By default a crash disables the check.

cli:-vrlinkforceenable.what: Testing switch: report VR Link (streaming VR to a headset) as available regardless of platform or video encoder.

cli:-vronly.what: Legacy Steam UI switch, probably a VR-only startup mode with no desktop UI. It is registered next to the old `-opengl` UI renderer switches.

cli:-vrskip.what: Skip VR initialization entirely, no matter which component asks for it.

cli:-websocket.what: Connect to the Steam backend (CM servers) over WebSocket instead of TCP/UDP. Can help behind restrictive firewalls or proxies.

cli:-websocketignorecertissues.what: With `-websocket`, ignore TLS certificate validation errors on the WebSocket CM connection. Valve marks it as for dev use only.

cli:-windowed.what: Run Big Picture in a window instead of fullscreen. The bootstrapper also reads it to choose a windowed update UI.

concommand:achievement_clear.what: Developer console: clear one achievement for the current user, probably `achievement_clear <appid> <achievement_api_name>`. The argument format is not in the help; `reset_all_stats` is the 'clear everything' variant.

concommand:app_backup.what: Console: `app_backup <appId> <target folder> [max folder size MB]` writes a Steam backup of an installed app to a folder, split into files of the given size.

concommand:app_change_compat_tool.what: Console: `app_change_compat_tool <appid> <name> [config=]` sets the Steam Play compatibility tool (e.g. a Proton version's internal name) for an app, with an optional tool config string.

concommand:app_delay_update.what: Console: `app_delay_update <appid> <seconds>` holds back an app's pending update for the given number of seconds.

concommand:app_dlc_status.what: Console: `app_dlc_status <appId> <dlcId>` prints the install/ownership status of one DLC of an app.

concommand:app_download_enable.what: Console: `app_download_enable <0|1>` turns content downloads off or on globally.

concommand:app_info_find.what: Console: `app_info_find <path> <value>` lists apps whose appinfo has the key set to the value, e.g. `app_info_find common/type media`; `*` matches any value.

concommand:app_info_print.what: Console: `app_info_print <appid> [section]` dumps the cached appinfo (PICS) KeyValues of an app, optionally only one section such as `config` or `depots`.

concommand:app_info_update.what: Console: `app_info_update [0|1]` refreshes appinfo from the PICS servers; with 1 it updates all apps.

concommand:app_install.what: Console: `app_install <appId> [volumeindex]` starts installing an app, optionally into the library folder with that index (see `library_folder_list`).

concommand:app_installed_files.what: Console: `app_installed_files <AppID>` lists the files installed for an app.

concommand:app_license_request.what: Console: `app_license_request <AppID>` asks for a free license for an app the account doesn't own yet (free-to-play/free apps).

concommand:app_mark_validation.what: Console: `app_mark_validation <appId> <0|1>` marks an app as needing file validation; 1 requests a full validation.

concommand:app_move.what: Console: `app_move <appId> <volumeindex>` moves an installed app to another library folder, given by its volume index.

concommand:app_set_config.what: Console: `app_set_config <AppID> <key> <value>` sets a per-app config value in the client's app config.

concommand:app_start_validation.what: Console: `app_start_validation <appId>` starts verifying the integrity of an app's files, like 'Verify integrity of game files'.

concommand:app_status.what: Console: `app_status <appId>` prints install state, size, update and download status for an app.

concommand:app_stop.what: Console: `app_stop <appid> [force:0|1]` stops a running app; with `1` it forces termination.

concommand:app_update_cancel.what: Console: `app_update_cancel <EAppUpdateError>` cancels the running app update, taking the EAppUpdateError code to report as the reason. Mainly a debug command.

concommand:app_update_status.what: Console: `app_update_status [appId]` prints update/download progress for one app, or for all apps that are updating.

concommand:apps_installed.what: Console: list all installed apps with their IDs and install status.

concommand:apps_running.what: Console: show the running games Steam tracks (app IDs, processes).

concommand:async_disconnect.what: Console debug command: disconnect from the Steam CM server asynchronously, to test reconnect handling.

concommand:build_installer.what: Console: `build_installer <project file> <target folder> [beta key] [beta pwd]` builds a retail/backup installer from a project file, optionally from a beta branch.

concommand:cloud_file_exists.what: Console: `cloud_file_exists <appid> <root> <file>` checks whether a file exists in an app's Steam Cloud storage under the given root.

concommand:cloud_get_file_info.what: Console: `cloud_get_file_info <appid> <index> [bExternalAPI=1]` prints info about the Nth Steam Cloud file of an app.

concommand:cloud_get_num_files.what: Console: `cloud_get_num_files <appid> [bExternalAPI=1]` prints how many Steam Cloud files an app has.

concommand:cloud_sync_app.what: Console: `cloud_sync_app <appid>` runs the background Steam Cloud sync for an app.

concommand:cloud_sync_down.what: Console: `cloud_sync_down <appid>` runs the on-launch Steam Cloud sync for an app, which downloads newer cloud saves.

concommand:cloud_sync_up.what: Console: `cloud_sync_up <appid>` runs the after-game Steam Cloud sync for an app, which uploads saves.

concommand:cm_force_change.what: Console: drop the current Connection Manager and switch to another CM server from the list.

concommand:compute_file_sha.what: Console: `compute_file_sha <path>` computes and prints the SHA-1 of a file on disk.

concommand:config_refresh.what: Console: reload the client configuration (config/convars from the server/config store) without restarting.

concommand:connect_remote.what: Console: `connect_remote <ip:port>` connects to a Remote Play / In-Home Streaming host at that address.

concommand:controller_calibration_stage.what: Console: `controller_calibration_stage <stage> [controller index]` sends a calibration-stage message to the controller hardware (factory calibration/testing).

concommand:disable_license.what: Console (Steamworks developers): `disable_license <packageid>` temporarily disables a license granted through the Steamworks partner site, so you can test as a non-owner.

concommand:download_chunk.what: Console: `download_chunk <appid> <depotid> <sha>` downloads one content chunk from a depot.

concommand:download_depot.what: Console: `download_depot <appid> <depotid> [<target manifestid>] [<delta manifestid>]` downloads one depot, optionally a specific (older) manifest. Commonly used to fetch old game versions; output lands under `steamapps/content/app_<id>/depot_<id>`.

concommand:download_sources.what: Console: print the list of content download sources (CDN/cache servers) in use.

concommand:dump_box_ips.what: Console: print the local IP addresses the client has detected on this machine.

concommand:dump_offline_playtime.what: Console: print the playtime sessions recorded locally while offline, which are later reported to the server.

concommand:dump_scheduled_functions.what: Console: list the client's internal scheduled function/callback timers.

concommand:enable_license.what: Console (Steamworks developers): `enable_license <packageid>` re-enables a license that was turned off with `disable_license`.

concommand:find.what: Console: `find <substring>` lists console commands and convars whose names or help contain the text.

concommand:gamestream_debug.what: Console: `gamestream_debug <0|1>` turns verbose game-streaming (Remote Play) debug logging on or off.

concommand:gamestream_fail.what: Console debug command: force the current game-stream session to fail, to test error handling.

concommand:get_download_throttle.what: Console: print the current download bandwidth limit (see `set_download_throttle`).

concommand:gr_enum_audio.what: Console (game recording): list the audio sessions/sources that game recording can capture.

concommand:gr_write_json.what: Console (game recording): write the game-recording metadata JSON (clip timeline: time, duration).

concommand:http_cache_clearall.what: Console: delete all cached data from the client's internal HTTP client and the CEF browser cache.

concommand:http_test.what: Console: `http_test [url]` tests HTTP connectivity with a request to the given URL (or a default one).

concommand:httpclients.what: Console: print statistics for the client's HTTP clients.

concommand:jobs.what: Console: `jobs [group_by_attribute]` lists the active internal jobs (async tasks) in this process, optionally grouped.

concommand:library_asset_cache_print.what: Console: `library_asset_cache_print <appid>` prints the cached library artwork (capsule, hero, logo with logo_position) for an app.

concommand:library_asset_cache_recheck.what: Console: `library_asset_cache_recheck <appid>` checks an app's cached library artwork again and refetches it, e.g. to fix missing or stale capsule images.

concommand:library_folder_add.what: Console: `library_folder_add <path>` adds a directory as a Steam library folder.

concommand:library_folder_list.what: Console: list all mounted Steam library folders (volumes) with their indexes. These indexes are what `app_install`/`app_move` take as `volumeindex`.

concommand:licenses_for_app.what: Console: `licenses_for_app <appid>` lists the account's active licenses (packages) that grant the app.

concommand:licenses_print.what: Console: list all licenses (packages) owned by the logged-in account.

concommand:log_callbacks.what: Console: `log_callbacks <first callbackID> [last callbackID]` logs Steam API callbacks with IDs in the range as they are posted.

concommand:log_ipc.what: Console: `log_ipc [counts|verbose|#maxcount] <filter>` turns on logging of IPC calls between Steam processes and games, filtered by name. The default mode is `counts`.

concommand:manifest_dump.what: Console: `manifest_dump <filename> [0|1]` prints the contents of a depot manifest file; with 1 it also lists the chunks.

concommand:mem_stats.what: Console: print memory allocation statistics for the steamclient process.

concommand:mem_validate.what: Console: `mem_validate <dump|leaks> <threshold>` runs a memory validation pass in the Steam UI process and dumps allocations or reports leaks above the threshold.

concommand:mem_walk.what: Console: `mem_walk [full]` walks and validates the heap; `full` does a complete pass.

concommand:@metricsDisabledCatalogs.what: Not an ordinary command: a server/config-driven setting (`@` prefix) holding a comma-separated list of metrics catalogs to disable. It is checked last, after the enabled/disabled operation lists.

concommand:@metricsDisabledOperations.what: Config-driven setting (`@` prefix): a comma-separated list of metrics operations to disable. It has the highest priority over the other metrics settings, including `@bMetricsEnabled`.

concommand:@metricsEnabledOperations.what: Config-driven setting (`@` prefix): a comma-separated list of metrics operations to enable even if their catalog is in `@metricsDisabledCatalogs`.

concommand:minidump_assert.what: Console debug command: trigger an assert so the assert/minidump reporting path runs.

concommand:minidump_crash.what: Console debug command: crash the Steam client on purpose, to test crash dumps and reporting.

concommand:net_fake_state.what: Console: `net_fake_state <normal|NoLAN|CaptivePortal_Redirected|CaptivePortal_InPlace|NoInternet|NoSteam>` simulates network conditions to test offline and captive-portal UI. Use `normal` to restore. The `-net_fake_state` switch sets the startup value.

concommand:net_msgdump.what: Console: print the list of network messages sent to the Steam backend.

concommand:net_msgspew.what: Console: log every sent and received Steam network (CM) message as it happens.

concommand:open.what: Console: `open <internal url>` opens a main Steam navigation page, like `steam://open/<page>` (e.g. `open games`, `open settings`). The argument format is assumed.

concommand:p2p_info.what: Console: print the current state of the P2P networking subsystem (sessions, relays).

concommand:package_info_print.what: Console: `package_info_print <packageid>` prints the cached package info (apps, depots, license type) for a package (sub).

concommand:patch_dump.what: Console: `patch_dump <filename> <depotid>` prints the contents of a depot delta-patch file.

concommand:peer_content_server_status.what: Console: print the status of the local peer content server, the LAN game-transfer server that listens on TCP port 27040 by default.

concommand:print_sdr_ping.what: Console: print this client's Steam Datagram Relay (SDR) ping-location string, i.e. the measured relay latencies used for matchmaking.

concommand:profile.what: Console: `profile <seconds>` runs the vprof profiler in the Steam UI process for N seconds.

concommand:profile_dump.what: Console: dump the full vprof profile of all threads. If vprof is off, it uses the last collected data.

concommand:profile_on_dump_spikes.what: Console: `profile_on_dump_spikes <ms>` starts vprof and automatically dumps any frame that takes longer than the threshold in milliseconds. Stop with `profile_off`.

concommand:profile_show_gui.what: Console: open a vprof profile window for each known thread. Data collection still needs `profile_on`/`profile_off`.

concommand:protobuf_parse_stats.what: Console: `protobuf_parse_stats [reset]` prints a histogram of parsed protobuf message body sizes and how many were parsed on worker threads; `reset` clears the counters. Related settings: `@bProtobufParseTimeProfile`, `@bAssertOnProtoBufBodyMismatch`.

concommand:quit.what: Console: `quit [force|now|system]` exits the Steam client. Without an argument it exits safely; `force`/`now` skip waiting; `system` is probably a system-initiated exit such as a shutdown.

concommand:remote_client_dongle.what: Console: controls a Remote Play/Steam Link wireless dongle. Syntax: `remote_client_dongle [[connect] clientid ssid password] | disconnect | status | disable | enable | leddebug | lednodebug | verbose 0|1 | debugpdthresh <thres>` (default threshold -75).

concommand:remote_client_softapcmd.what: Console: `remote_client_softapcmd <args>` sends a raw command to the soft access point used for direct Remote Play / Steam Link connections.

concommand:remote_clients.what: Console: print information about Remote Play / In-Home Streaming clients found on the LAN.

concommand:render_ipc_connections.what: Console: list or draw the active IPC connections between Steam and connected processes.

concommand:reset_all_stats.what: Console (developer): clear all stats and achievements for the current user, probably `reset_all_stats <appid>`.

concommand:serverbrowser_debug_toggle.what: Console: turn debug logging for the game server browser (master server queries) on or off.

concommand:serverbrowser_debug_verbose.what: Console: turn on verbose debug logging for the server browser. Valve's help string is the same as for `serverbrowser_debug_toggle`.

concommand:service_repair.what: Console: repair the Steam Client Service. Windows only; no effect on Linux.

concommand:service_restart.what: Console: restart the Steam Client Service. Windows only.

concommand:service_test.what: Console: test that the Steam Client Service works. Windows only.

concommand:set_display_state.what: Console: `set_display_state <eState>` forces the display into a given state (a numeric display-state enum, e.g. on/off/dimmed on SteamOS). Used to test display power handling.

concommand:set_download_throttle.what: Console: `set_download_throttle <kbps> [bPersistent]` limits download bandwidth in kbps. 0 is probably unlimited; with a true second argument the limit is saved across sessions.

concommand:set_spew.what: Console: `set_spew <group> <spewlevel> <loglevel>` sets the console-spew and log-file levels for one logging group.

concommand:set_spew_level.what: Console: `set_spew_level <spewlevel> <loglevel>` sets the console-spew and log-file levels for all logging groups.

concommand:set_var.what: Console: `set_var <name> <value>` sets the value of a console variable (convar).

concommand:shader_build.what: Console: `shader_build <appId> [threadCount]` compiles an app's pre-cached shaders (Fossilize replay) now, optionally with that many threads.

concommand:shader_process.what: Console: `shader_process <appId> <bucketID> [overrideBasePath]` processes one shader-cache bucket for an app, optionally from a different base path.

concommand:shader_prune.what: Console: delete stale or unneeded shader cache data.

concommand:shader_scan.what: Console: `shader_scan <appId> [overridePath]` scans an app's shader cache, optionally from another path.

concommand:stats_dump.what: Console: `stats_dump [filter]` prints the internal debug stats (counters) whose names match the filter.

concommand:stats_monitor.what: Console: `stats_monitor <stat name>` keeps watching one debug stat and shows its value as it changes.

concommand:stats_reset.what: Console: `stats_reset [filter]` sets matching debug stats back to 0.

concommand:test_concurrent_textfilter_ch.what: Console test command: queue several text-filter (chat profanity filter) setting changes for the UI at once, to test race handling.

concommand:test_dropcon.what: Console test command: drop the current Steam backend connection, to test reconnect behavior.

concommand:test_failnextconnect.what: Console test command: make the next connection attempt to the backend fail.

concommand:test_opus_voice_encode.what: Console test command: encode voice data with the Opus codec as a test.

concommand:test_os_suspend.what: Console test command (steamclient): simulate the OS announcing a system suspend.

concommand:test_reconnect.what: Console test command: reconnect after `test_failnextconnect` or `test_dropcon`.

concommand:test_resume.what: Console test command (steamclient): simulate resuming from a system suspend; pairs with `test_os_suspend`.

concommand:test_resume_from_suspend.what: Console test command (Steam UI): run the UI's resume-from-suspend handling.

concommand:test_suspend.what: Console test command (Steam UI): fake a system suspend event.

concommand:test_voice_encode.what: Console test command: encode voice data with the default/legacy voice codec as a test.

concommand:timed_trial_add_playtime.what: Console (developer only): `timed_trial_add_playtime <appId> <seconds>` adds playtime to a timed-trial app, to test trial expiry.

concommand:timed_trial_reset_playtime.what: Console (developer only): `timed_trial_reset_playtime <appId>` resets the playtime used on a timed-trial app.

concommand:timed_trial_status.what: Console: `timed_trial_status <appId>` shows the timed-trial status (time allowed and used) for an app.

concommand:toggle_idle_suspend_inhibit.what: Console: `toggle_idle_suspend_inhibit <delay>` toggles inhibiting idle suspend after the given delay, to test SteamOS idle-suspend handling.

concommand:user_friends.what: Console: print the logged-in user's friends list.

concommand:user_info.what: Console: print various information about the Steam session and user (account, login state).

concommand:verify_chunk_store.what: Console: `verify_chunk_store <appid> <depotid> <datafile>` checks a depot chunk store / data file. Valve's help text ('run app depot build as specified in appbuildfile') looks copied from another command, so the exact behavior is uncertain.

concommand:vgui_spewpanelstats.what: Console: print statistics about the active VGUI panels (counts per type), for the legacy VGUI UI.

concommand:voice_game_usage.what: Console: show how the running game uses Steam Voice (ISteamUser voice APIs).

concommand:workshop_download_item.what: Console: `workshop_download_item <appid> <PublishedFileId>` downloads a Workshop item. Works like `download_item` and is commonly used to fetch mods manually.

concommand:workshop_status.what: Console: `workshop_status <appId>` prints the Workshop subscription and download status for an app's items.
